learningObjective: Given one state lattice, distinguish how forward-backward forms a posterior for a state at one timestep from how Viterbi forms one globally consistent state path.
mediumRationale: A deterministic two-panel SVG is the smallest medium that can hold the chain topology fixed while changing only the dynamic-programming objective. The first panel makes the left and right summaries meet at one state; the second makes predecessor storage and reverse backtracking visible as one connected path.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected: automatic graph layout would not reliably align identical timestep-state lattices or preserve the compact left-versus-right and backtracking geometry at phone width.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected: deterministic coordinates keep the same three-state, four-timestep lattice aligned across both objectives and make direction, selected state, path continuity, and backtracking explicit.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: a DP table could compare sum and max cells, but it would not show that a marginal joins all compatible prefixes and suffixes while a decoded sequence must remain connected across time.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: changing transition scores could demonstrate different winners, but controls and state are unnecessary for the invariant distinction between a per-timestep marginal and a global path.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the reviewed IEEE papers and textbook contain useful HMM trellises and algorithm presentations, but no permissive figure-reuse license was established. The shipped lattice, wording, geometry, and teaching comparison are original.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: the equations specify each recurrence, yet readers must mentally align two opposite passes and understand why independent per-timestep posterior maxima are not equivalent to backtracking one feasible Viterbi path.

pages.insight: The preceding Message Passing slide describes local sum-product messages moving forward and backward through a chain, providing the general inference context but conflating message passing with EM and showing no HMM trellis.
The GMM/HMM slide separates evaluation, decoding, and training: it assigns the forward or backward algorithm to evaluation, Viterbi to decoding, and forward-backward inside Baum-Welch to training.

The directly relevant Forward-Backward slide explains that conditioning on the state at time k separates the observations on its two sides, so cached forward and backward terms can be multiplied to obtain a state posterior. Its adjacent Baum-Welch column places that inference inside EM.

The following linear-chain CRF slide applies dynamic-programming caches and log-space normalization to dependent sequence labels, corroborating the modern structured-prediction use without comparing state marginals to Viterbi backtracking.

deckReview.notes: The complete 214-page local deck was text-indexed for forward-backward, Viterbi, hidden Markov models, HMM, message passing, and dynamic programming. Pages 67-70 form the only directly relevant contiguous neighborhood and were read in full. Page 69 supplies the key two-sided conditional-independence insight, but the deck does not spatially compare marginal inference with global path decoding. No slide pixels, wording, formulas, coordinates, or embedded artwork are reused.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is that both algorithms traverse the same exponentially large path space with the same table shape but return different objects. Forward-backward combines sums of all compatible prefixes and suffixes at each state, whereas Viterbi keeps a maximizing predecessor for each partial endpoint and later follows those linked choices backward. The schematic uses no empirical values or source-specific figure structure.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages, inspected the exact pages 67-70 neighborhood, and checked the primary Viterbi paper, the canonical IEEE HMM tutorial, and an authoritative MIT Press textbook before selecting an original same-lattice comparison.

implementation.accessibility: Each panel has a linked title and complete description. State letters, timestep labels, opposing arrowheads, a double-ring target, line thickness, a continuous selected path, and a labelled backtracking arrow carry the lesson independently of color. The established two-panel primitive stacks below 640 pixels; each panel uses a compact 300-pixel viewBox with no minimum width, keeping labels readable at 390 CSS pixels. Existing theme variables provide dark-mode contrast, and shared print rules force a light high-contrast palette and avoid breaks inside the figure.
